hints: Take away the root of a full tree. What do the left and right parts look like, and how many nodes can each have?
Recursion with memoization: shapes(m) = for each odd left size i, combine every left shape of i nodes with every right shape of m−1−i nodes as "x" + left + right. Even m has no shapes.

1. If m is even, return an empty list; if m == 1, return ["o"].
  2. If m is already in the memo, return it.
  3. For i = 1, 3, …, m−2: for each left in shapes(i) and right in shapes(m−1−i), add "x" + left + right.
  4. Store the list in the memo and return it.

approaches.name: Plain recursion
approaches.idea: Split the remaining nodes between left and right subtrees and recurse, rebuilding the same smaller sizes many times.

approaches.name: Optimal: memoized recursion
approaches.idea: Each size m is built once and reused. Total work is about the size of all generated strings.
approaches.time: O(C<sub>n/2</sub> · n) (Catalan number of shapes, each length n)

explain: For n = 5, the root uses one node and the other 4 split as (1, 3) or (3, 1). With a 1-node left and the 3-node "xoo" on the right we get "xoxoo"; the reverse split gives "xxooo". Every full tree has an odd number of nodes, so n = 4 returns []. The preorder string is built as the root's letter, then the left string, then the right string. This order also makes the shapes distinct, because different shapes give different strings.
recognize: 'List every structure of size n' where a structure splits into two smaller ones → recursive generation with memo by size.
